title: Hybrid-lane conductor: precision-aware attention dispatch and prefill throttling
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem: Our current serving runtime picks kernel implementations independently per operator which leads to cross-operator precision mismatches, extra dequant/requant copies, and poor scheduling for long-prefill requests. For INT8/FP8 mixed workloads we observe a ~12-18% token throughput regression on middle-length (256-1024) sequences and a 6-12ms tail latency increase for chat-style prefill + decode flows.

Goal: Implement a precision-aware dispatch layer (the 'hybrid-lane conductor') that groups ops into execution lanes by end-to-end numeric path (FP32, FP16, INT8, FP8-accelerated paths), inserts minimal on-the-fly reprojection, and schedules prefill work with lane-affinity to minimize dequant/requant churn and attention-kernel stalls. The feature should reduce cross-operator dequant overhead, improve KV-prefill overlap, and provide a knob to trade latency vs. unit-cost for mixed-precision models.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime adds a lane assignment pass at compile/graph-walk time which tags operator groups with a precision lane
End-to-end E2E benchmark against baseline shows >=7% throughput improvement for mixed INT8/FP8 model on 256-1024 sequences or no regression on single-precision workloads
Prefill scheduling reduces observed dequant memory copies by >=50% on mixed-precision traces
No functional regressions: outputs within existing acceptance thresholds for sampled prompts (existing eval buckets)
Feature gated by runtime flag and default-off for private/Dedicated until gradual rollout
technical_notes: Design constraints: must keep kernel selection decisions localizable to avoid global solver cost, rely on existing operator fusion pipeline, and leverage KV-cache-aware batching. The conductor will not automatically change model weights or quantization parameters; it will select compatible kernels and insert compact reprojection ops only when lane crossing is unavoidable. We'll reuse the existing kernel-capability database and extend it with lane compatibility vectors. Prefill scheduling uses a lightweight lane-token budget heuristic to decide when to delay lower-priority lanes to maintain decoder tail SLOs.
implementation_plan: Spec: define lane types and compatibility matrix (FP32/FP16, FP8-soft, INT8-zero-point) — doc at https://redwood.app/confluence/runtime/hybrid-lane-spec
Compiler: add graph-walk pass to compute lane tags and annotate operator groups
Runtime: extend scheduler to accept lane-affinity and a lane budget per worker; implement reprojection op insertion and zero-copy where supported
Kernels: add lightweight FP8->FP16 reprojection primitive (fused scaling + clamp) and an INT8 passthrough wrapper for attention kernels
Benchmarks: create mixed-precision trace corpus (chat+completion), integrate into perf CI
Feature gate: add runtime flag and console toggle; default-off for private until signed off
Rollout: Canary on hosted with 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with metric checks
test_plan: Unit tests for lane assignment logic and compatibility matrix
Microbenchmarks for reprojection primitive latency and memory allocs
End-to-end perf test on p4d and g5 instances with representative models (redwood-compat-catalog reference models)
Regression tests: run existing eval sets against baseline and new runtime and compare token-level divergence thresholds
Chaos test: force cross-lane pressure and validate fallback correctness and safety
metrics: Average decode tail latency (p95) for chat prefill+decode - target no regression
Number of dequant/requant memory copies per request - target <=50% of baseline
CPU/GPU utilization and allocator churn during prefill windows
Cost per million tokens (estimate) for INT8/FP8 mixed workloads
